item.title: Re: +100
item.content:encoded:
+ Technical miscellanies regarding a dynamic date
- Conceal

It's messy as can be, but if you swap out this:

 [[size 75%]]##grey|by Administrator on 5 May 2020, 15:43##[[/size]]

with this:

 [[html]]<span style="font-family:verdana,arial,helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:0.60em;color: grey">by Administrator on <span id="dateTime"></span><script>var d = new Date(); var months = ["January", "February", "March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "August", "September", "October", "November", "December"]; document.getElementById("dateTime").innerHTML = (d.getDate() + 1) + " " + months[d.getMonth()] + " " + d.getFullYear() + ", 15:43";</script></span>[[/html]]

it'll hopefully be along the lines of what you're looking for. I assumed the 15:43 time was of significance, but that can be adjusted to be dynamic if needed.

It seems to work fine on the site proper, but fails on the sandbox (presumably some form of JavaScript permissions?). Tested for functionality in IE, Firefox, Chrome, and mobile Safari.

+ I also have something put together to make the inline "fourteen-year run" dynamic, if you're willing to compromise on text vs. digit
- Enshroud

Swapping out:

  It is regretful to announce that in two weeks time, we will need to shut down Wikidot. We thank the community for sticking with us for all these years, though we do understand that you may have lots of questions regarding the nature of why we are choosing to shut down after a fourteen-year run.

(Note: this won't work unless you delete the two indents at the start of that paragraph. Your guess is as good as mine.)

with

 [[html]]<span style="font-family:verdana,arial,helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:0.80em">It is regretful to announce that in two weeks time, we will need to shut down Wikidot. We thank the community for sticking with us for all these years, though we do understand that you may have lots of questions regarding the nature of why we are choosing to shut down after a <span id="years"></span> year run.</span><script>var dStart = new Date('2006-08-01 00:00');var dCurrent = new Date();document.getElementById("years").innerHTML = dCurrent.getYear() - dStart.getYear();</script>[[/html]]

would give you "12 year run" corresponding to the current date.

item.title: Author's Note

Thanks to TwistedGears for the prompt last night, and for TwistedGears, Randomini, Sound Chaser, and Dr_Leonard for looking it over and reviewing it, and for Tagliafierro for giving me the title!
